questions.question: Distinguish the members of the budget family and the zero-based method from incremental budgeting.
questions.expected_answer: The cash budget forecasts money in, money out and the surviving balance month by month — the survival question. The capital budget schedules long-term asset purchases with amounts, timing and funding, feeding the cash budget its landing dates. Medium-term budgets plan one to three years (expansion, staffing); long-term budgets carry strategy further in broader strokes. Zero-based budgeting starts every line at nothing and demands fresh justification — what does it buy now, what breaks without it — unlike incremental budgeting, which copies last year plus a percentage and so carries dead costs forever.

questions.question: Build Thabo's three-month cash budget and explain the two cash-only rules it obeys.
questions.expected_answer: Receipts each month: cash sales R12 000 plus collection of the previous month's credit sales R8 000 (40% of R20 000) = R20 000. Payments: purchases R12 000, wages R3 000, rent R1 500 = R16 500; plus the machine R6 000 in February. January: surplus R3 500, opening R2 000, closing R5 500. February: deficit R2 500 (3 500 − 6 000), closing R3 000. March: surplus R3 500, closing R6 500. Cash-only rules: credit sales enter at COLLECTION, not sale; depreciation never appears, because no rand leaves — the cash budget records only actual money movements.

questions.question: Read the quarter for its three decisions/lessons.
questions.expected_answer: Timing: the R6 000 machine was deliberately placed in February where the balances could carry the dip to R3 000 — seen in advance it is manageable; unplanned it could have emptied the account, and a projected negative would prompt delaying the purchase or arranging an overdraft in advance. The lag: 40% of each month's earning arrives a month late, so growth months feel tight — profit and cash keep different calendars. Control: when actual figures arrive, each variance against budget (purchases above, sales below) becomes a specific investigation, catching problems while they are small.
